precepts.text: The account itself: Jael covered him with a mantle, gave him milk when he asked water, and when he was fast asleep and weary she smote the nail into his temples and fastened it into the ground; when Barak came, Sisera lay dead with the nail in his temples.
precepts.point: Blessed above women in the tent shall Jael the wife of Heber the Kenite be. Sisera asked water and she gave him milk; then she put her hand to the nail and her right hand to the workman's hammer, and where he bowed, there he fell down dead.

note.label: Judges 5: The Song of Deborah and Barak: A Willing People

precepts.why:
The song is singing the account of chapter 4. “Jael went out to meet Sisera, and said unto him, Turn in, my lord, turn in to me; fear not. And when he had turned in unto her into the tent, she covered him with a mantle.” He asked, “Give me, I pray thee, a little water to drink; for I am thirsty. And she opened a bottle of milk, and gave him drink, and covered him.” That is the song's “He asked water, and she gave him milk.”

Sisera told her to stand in the door and say no man was there. “Then Jael Heber’s wife took a nail of the tent, and took an hammer in her hand, and went softly unto him, and smote the nail into his temples, and fastened it into the ground: for he was fast asleep and weary. So he died.” That is the hand to the nail and the right hand to the workmen's hammer, and “where he bowed, there he fell down dead.”

Then, “as Barak pursued Sisera, Jael came out to meet him, and said unto him, Come, and I will shew thee the man whom thou seekest. And when he came into her tent, behold, Sisera lay dead, and the nail was in his temples.” For this she is “Blessed above women”, “blessed shall she be above women in the tent.”

precepts.text: Sisera the captain fled from the battle and died by the hand of a woman when Jael smote the nail into his temples.
precepts.point: He reigned only three years. Killing his seventy brothers bought him a three year reign and a crushed skull; it was to no profit. If you are doing wickedness behind closed doors and think the Most High does not see it, he sees it, and he brings swift judgment.

note.label: Judges 9: Abimelech and the Fire Out of the Bramble

precepts.why:
Abimelech begs his armourbearer, “Draw thy sword, and slay me, that men say not of me, A woman slew him.” It was counted a shame for a man of war to die by the hand of a woman, and it had happened earlier in this book. Sisera the captain fled from the battle, and “Jael Heber’s wife took a nail of the tent, and took an hammer in her hand, and went softly unto him, and smote the nail into his temples, and fastened it into the ground: for he was fast asleep and weary. So he died.”

Sisera died by the hand of a woman with a nail; Abimelech had his skull crushed by a woman with a millstone, and could only try to hide it by having a young man thrust him through.

points: When Ehud was dead, the children of Israel again did evil, and the Most High sold them into the hand of Jabin king of Canaan, that reigned in Hazor, whose captain was Sisera, which dwelt in Harosheth of the Gentiles.
Sisera had nine hundred chariots of iron, and twenty years he mightily oppressed the children of Israel, and they cried unto the Most High.

Deborah, a prophetess, the wife of Lapidoth, judged Israel at that time, dwelling under the palm tree of Deborah between Ramah and Bethel in mount Ephraim, and the children of Israel came up to her for judgment.

She calls Barak the son of Abinoam and gives him the commandment of the Most High: draw toward mount Tabor with ten thousand men of Naphtali and Zebulun, and I will draw unto thee Sisera with his chariots and his multitude to the river Kishon, and deliver him into thine hand.

Barak answers, if thou wilt go with me, then I will go, but if thou wilt not go with me, then I will not go. Deborah agrees to go, but tells him the journey shall not be for his honour, for the Most High shall sell Sisera into the hand of a woman.

Barak calls Zebulun and Naphtali to Kedesh and goes up with ten thousand men at his feet, and Deborah goes up with him. Heber the Kenite, of the children of Hobab the father in law of Moses, had severed himself from the Kenites and pitched his tent by Kedesh.

Sisera gathers all nine hundred chariots of iron unto the river of Kishon, and Deborah says unto Barak, up, for this is the day in which the Lord hath delivered Sisera into thine hand; is not the Lord gone out before thee?

The Most High discomfits Sisera and all his chariots and all his host with the edge of the sword before Barak; Sisera lights down off his chariot and flees away on his feet, and all his host falls upon the edge of the sword; there was not a man left.

Sisera flees on foot to the tent of Jael the wife of Heber the Kenite, for there was peace between Jabin the king of Hazor and the house of Heber. Jael invites him in, covers him with a mantle, and gives him milk to drink when he asks for water.

He tells her to stand in the door and say no man is there; then Jael takes a nail of the tent and a hammer in her hand, goes softly unto him as he sleeps fast and weary, and smites the nail into his temples and fastens it into the ground, and he dies. The word through Deborah stands: Sisera was sold into the hand of a woman.

When Barak comes pursuing, Jael shows him Sisera lying dead with the nail in his temples. So God subdued that day Jabin the king of Canaan before the children of Israel, and their hand prospered and prevailed until they had destroyed him.
